newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to sell repossessed ventures.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to sell repossessed ventures.

text.p: Sri Lankan president Chandrika Kumaratunga said on Saturday her government would restructure and sell seven privatised government enterprises it repossessed earlier this week due to alleged mismanagement.
"We will restructure them at government expense and re-privatise in accordance with the laws of the land," Kumaratunga told supporters at her Sri Lanka Freedom Party's annual convention in Colombo.
The government this week re-nationalised seven companies privatised by the previous United National Party (UNP) government, which ruled the country from 1977 to 1994.

It used the Rehabilitation of Public Enterprises Act to take over the companies for their "gross mismanagement and the plundering of assets and funds of the companies by their investors", a senior government official, speaking to Reuters on condition of anonymity, said.

The seven companies are Hingurana Sugar Industries Ltd., Kantalai Sugar Industries Ltd., Mattegama Textile Mills Ltd., graphite company Kahatagaha Mines Ltd., State Fertilizer Manufacturing Company, Sri Lanka State Trading (Hardware) Corporation and CCC Fertilizers Ltd.
Kumaratunga said more than 10,000 workers of the seven enterprises had lost their jobs since they were sold at virtually give away prices by the previous government.
She said the workers would be reinstated in their jobs and made productive by the restructuring process.

The Rehabilitation of Public Enterprises Act enables the government to repossess privatised state ventures, specially where there are threats to employee interests. The government has to compensate the original buyer.

Sri Lanka is restructuring or privatising loss making and badly run public enterprises, under a programme which includes getting private management into the country's national carrier and telecommunications operator.
Sri Lanka has advertised the sale of a 35 percent stake and management in Sri Lanka Telecom, and a 40 percent stake and managmenet of Air Lanka.
